plates.side_label: 31 OCT 1794 & 28 JUL 1844 DALTON AUTOPSY: PINK GERANIUM (450 NM BLUE + 650 NM RED) & 100% CLEAR VITREOUS HUMOUR
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked daylight vs candlelight spectral transmission diagram from John Dalton (31 October 1794 / 1798 Manchester Memoirs 5: 28–45) shows why a pink geranium (reflecting both short-wavelength blue ~450 nm and long-wavelength red ~650 nm) looked sky-blue to Dalton in blue-rich daylight but reddish in red-rich candlelight, alongside Joseph Ransome's 28 July 1844 autopsy finding of 100% clear vitreous humour.

teach_overlay.label: 1794 GERANIUM SPECTRUM & 28 JUL 1844 AUTOPSY: 100% CLEAR EYE JELLY DISPROVES DALTON'S BLUE-FILTER HYPOTHESIS
teach_overlay.detail: Inked daylight vs candlelight spectral transmission diagram on period paper from John Dalton (31 October 1794 / 1798 Manchester Memoirs 5: 28–45) showing why a pink geranium (reflecting both short-wavelength blue ~450 nm and long-wavelength red ~650 nm) looked sky-blue to Dalton in blue-rich daylight but reddish in red-rich candlelight, alongside Joseph Ransome's 28 July 1844 autopsy finding of 100% clear vitreous humour
teach_overlay.scale: John Dalton waited fifty years — from his seventeen ninety-four lecture to the day after his death in eighteen forty-four — so his doctor could look through the back of his own eyeball and prove his blue-jelly theory wrong
